exposure: maternal hemoglobin levels at admission (anemia, high hemoglobin, normal hemoglobin)
cohort: The study included 1,715 patients with preeclampsia with singleton pregnancies from a tertiary obstetrics and gynecology hospital.
finding: Both anemia and high hemoglobin levels at admission in patients with preeclampsia were related to increased risks of various adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes, although anemia was associated with a lower risk of SGA and NICU admission.
